thread:
Alex R: incident-bot paged oncall at 13:02 UTC — high queued requests to runtime; 500s for generation. link to incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4123
incident-bot: [auto] Pager triggered: high tail latency on /v1/generate (p95 > 3s) — paging eng-oncall
Maria K: I'm on it, popping into pager bridge. sharing timeline shortly.
Priya S: joining bridge. what's user visible impact? Maria, any customer-facing errors?
Alex R: Customer reports timeouts and slow streaming. Dashboard shows queued_count spike to 18k in us-east-1. Some hosts 100% GPU util.
Sam B: grabbing autoscale logs now. putting snippets below.
Sam B: ```
2026-03-15T12:58:41Z metric: queue_depth 100 -> 18000 within 4m
2026-03-15T12:59:05Z hpa: scale_event triggered replicas: 12 -> 12 (no-op due to limit)
2026-03-15T12:59:21Z pool: gpu_pool_us_east saturated nodes_available=0 pending_warmups=34
2026-03-15T13:00:02Z warmup: warmup_latency median=21s mean=28.7s
```
Maria K: key bit: HPA stuck due to maxReplicas cap from a previous commit. we're hitting pool hard and warmups are slow. Hypothesis 1: HPA limit too low so new pods can't come up. Hypothesis 2: Warmup latency due to quantized model loading on these nodes -> cold starts long.
Priya S: adding telemetry traces and targeted logs to the bridge. Also past 2 hours we saw a config change to autoscaler in us-east-1: `max_replicas: 12` (PR #789). Sam, can you confirm if burst capacity is allowed?
Sam B: burst_capacity flag is false for this pool. Manual uplift needed. I'm going to manually request a scale override to 20 replicas and force-provision 5 nodes.
Alex R: please annotate actions in thread. tagging @ops-bot for node provisioning.
ops-bot: node_provision_request accepted: provision_nodes(region=us-east-1,count=5,priority=high) request_id=prov-9821
Priya S: mitigation path: 1) force-provision 5 nodes (submitted), 2) temporarily raise max_replicas to 25 in HPA, 3) enable burst_capacity true, 4) route low-latency customers to dedicated warm pool (if available) 5) reduce batch_timeout to 25ms.
Maria K: executed temporary HPA patch: `kubectl apply -f hpa-temp.yaml` linking gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/temporary-hpa
Sam B: provisioning progress: 3/5 nodes up, kube join ok, but warmup still slow — new nodes showing warmup latency ~19s.
Alex R: customer impact note: enterprise customer "DataMuse" saw 40% request failures for 7m window. We should prepare incident page and customer outreach.
Priya S: collecting full timeline. Current working timeline entries:
- 12:56: queue_depth starts rising
- 12:58 autoscaler hit maxReplicas=12 (no new pods)
- 12:59 pool fully saturated, pending_warmups increase
- 13:02 pager fired (p95>3s)
- 13:05 manual provision request submitted
- 13:09 HPA patched to 25
- 13:12 additional nodes joined, queue depth falling
- 13:20 incident considered mitigated (p95 back to 700ms)
Maria K: next steps for RCA: gather autoscaler config, git history for PR #789, warmup logs for model-quantized path, and any kernel OOMs on nodes. I'll own RCA doc skeleton.
Sam B: logs uploaded to s3: s3://redwood-ops/incidents/INC-4123/autoscaler-logs.tar.gz
Alex R: assigning action items:
- Maria K: RCA doc + customer timeline
- Sam B: collect warmup traces + node kernel logs
- Priya S: verify feature flags (burst_capacity) and propose guardrails to prevent HPA hard caps without burst enabled
- Alex R: coordinate customer comms and legal notification
Priya S: quick wins: default maxReplicas should be >= required for 95th percentile load; add monitor that alerts if queue_depth > 1000 while replicas==maxReplicas.
Maria K: noted. will include mitigation checklist and postmortem owners.
ops-bot: incident INC-4123 status updated -> mitigated (post-incident review required)
Alex R: thanks all — prepping bridge notes for handoff to oncall-rotation for full RCA.
